session.question: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?
session.answer:
The study compared five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: weighted sum model (WSM), technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS), preference ranking organization method for enrichment evaluations (PROMETHEE), elimination and choice translating reality (ELECTRE), and data envelopment analysis (DEA). It assessed 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)

The sensitivity analysis varied criteria weights in several ways, including individual changes across the stability range of alternatives, fixed individual weight changes to observe effects on average scores, and a comparison of AHP-based weights with equal weights. It showed that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analysis of district heating systems, but they differ in how calculations are performed and how results are interpreted. A generalized algorithm for energy-sector sustainability assessment was also proposed. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-fee43646: The paper compares five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA. It evaluates 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria and performs sensitivity analysis by varying criteria weights in several ways, including individual changes and comparing AHP-based weights with equal weights. The sensitivity analysis, together with the literature review, indicates that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analyses of district heating systems, but they differ in how calculations are carried out and how results are interpreted.
From Jānis Daugavietis, Raimonda Soloha, Elīna Dāce, and Jeļena Ziemele. A comparison of multi-criteria decision analysis methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15072411, doi:10.3390/en15072411.

pqac-2291c40e: The paper compares five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for district heating sustainability assessment: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA. It evaluates 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria and performs sensitivity analysis by varying criteria weights in three ways: individually across the range of stability for alternatives, individually by a fixed value to see effects on average scores, and comparing AHP weights with equal weights. The study concludes that all methods are suitable for sustainability analysis of district heating systems, but they differ in calculation procedures and interpretation of results. It also provides a generalized algorithm for energy-sector sustainability assessment.
From Jānis Daugavietis, Raimonda Soloha, Elīna Dāce, and Jeļena Ziemele. A comparison of multi-criteria decision analysis methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15072411, doi:10.3390/en15072411.

pqac-39831f6e: The paper evaluates solar district heating systems (SDHS) for nearly zero energy buildings using a sustainability analysis covering technical, economic, environmental, and social aspects. It proposes a machine-learning-based framework combining multi-objective optimization and multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) to create a sustainability index for stakeholders and policymakers. The study compares retrofitted residential communities of different sizes in Emmen, Netherlands, against a decentralized heat pump. Results show SDHS can reach up to 95% solar fraction, and NZEB is economically viable only from 100 houses upward. It reports environmental and social improvements of 78.2% and 29.7% over heat pumps.
From Mohamed Hany Abokersh, Sachin Gangwar, Marleen Spiekman, Manel Vallès, Laureano Jiménez, and Dieter Boer. Sustainability insights on emerging solar district heating technologies to boost the nearly zero energy building concept. Renewable Energy, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2021.08.091, doi:10.1016/j.renene.2021.08.091.

pqac-aaf9894f: The excerpt describes a 2023 case study on sustainable supplier evaluation using several MCDA methods in a fuzzy environment: ARAS, EDAS, MAIRCA, TOPSIS, and VIKOR. The study focuses on sensitivity analysis to compare how these methods behave when evaluating battery suppliers. It reports that the methods produced similar ranking results, supported by the WS similarity measure and weighted Spearman correlation. The sensitivity analysis also identified the most important criteria as transportation cost, delivery time, and warranty period. This suggests the paper is useful for understanding MCDA method suitability, ranking consistency, and criteria influence in sustainability-related assessments.
From Jakub Więckowski, Bartłomiej Kizielewicz, Andrii Shekhovtsov, and Wojciech Sałabun. How do the criteria affect sustainable supplier evaluation? - a case study using multi-criteria decision analysis methods in a fuzzy environment. Journal of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.56578/jemse020102, doi:10.56578/jemse020102.

pqac-9182d68e: The paper discusses life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA) interpretation using multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), specifically PROMETHEE as an outranking method. It emphasizes that thresholds are important to distinguish indifference from preference and proposes a new way to set thresholds based on uncertainty in life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) methods. A case study on sustainable industrial hydrogen production compares three European locations and shows PROMETHEE can help derive a clear solution from differing environmental, economic, and social results. The excerpt highlights that comparing newly specified thresholds with default thresholds improves interpretation of LCSA results.
From Christina Wulf, Petra Zapp, Andrea Schreiber, and Wilhelm Kuckshinrichs. Setting thresholds to define indifferences and preferences in promethee for life cycle sustainability assessment of european hydrogen production. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13137009, doi:10.3390/su13137009.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes a 2021 study that assessed the sustainability of wastewater treatment techniques in urban Iraq using multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), specifically the weighted sum model (WSM). It evaluated 13 operating plants in 10 provinces with input from 52 specialists. Four treatment techniques were compared: conventional treatment, oxidation ditches, aeration lagoons, and membrane bioreactor (MBR). Sustainability was measured across environmental, social, economic, and technical dimensions using 11, 5, 7, and 4 indicators, respectively. Results ranked MBR highest, followed by oxidation ditches, aeration lagoons, and conventional treatment. Environmental factors contributed most; technical factors contributed least.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes a comparative evaluation of multi-criteria decision analysis methods for sustainable transport, not district heating. It reviews applications of MCDM/MCDA methods and then applies a hybrid approach (DEMATEL, REMBRANDT, VIKOR) to select an expressway route in north-eastern Poland. The results are compared with an environmental impact assessment report and with other methods mentioned in the literature review, including AHP, Fuzzy AHP, TOPSIS, and PROMETHEE. The paper focuses on ranking and multi-dimensional evaluation of popular MCDA methods in transport, but does not mention district heating, sustainability assessment details, sensitivity analysis, calculation differences, or interpretation related to district heating.

contexts.context: The paper discusses life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA) interpretation using multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), specifically PROMETHEE as an outranking method. It emphasizes that thresholds are important to distinguish indifference from preference and proposes a new way to set thresholds based on uncertainty in life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) methods. A case study on sustainable industrial hydrogen production compares three European locations and shows PROMETHEE can help derive a clear solution from differing environmental, economic, and social results. The excerpt highlights that comparing newly specified thresholds with default thresholds improves interpretation of LCSA results.

A comparison of multi-criteria decision analysis methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15072411, doi:10.3390/en15072411.
session.formatted_answer:
Question: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?

The study compared five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: weighted sum model (WSM), technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS), preference ranking organization method for enrichment evaluations (PROMETHEE), elimination and choice translating reality (ELECTRE), and data envelopment analysis (DEA). It assessed 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)

The sensitivity analysis varied criteria weights in several ways, including individual changes across the stability range of alternatives, fixed individual weight changes to observe effects on average scores, and a comparison of AHP-based weights with equal weights. It showed that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analysis of district heating systems, but they differ in how calculations are performed and how results are interpreted. A generalized algorithm for energy-sector sustainability assessment was also proposed. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)
